div.l: That eche of you to short with youre wey
In this viage shalle telle tales twey
To Caunterbury warde I mene it so .
And homeward he shalle telle oþ̉er talles to
Of aventures that whilom haue befalle
And whiche of you bereth hym best of alle
That is to sey that telleth in this case
Tales of the best sentence and most solace
Shalle haue a sopere of oure alther cost
Here in this place sittynge by this post
When that ye come ayen from caunterbury
And for to make you the more mery
I wille me solfe go wᵗith you and ryde
Ryight at myn owne cost and be your gide
And who that wille my iugement with sey
Shortly shalle pay alle that is spent by the wey
And yf ye vochesaff that hit be soo
Telle me anone withouten wordes moo
And I wille hertly shape me therfore
This thynge was graunted and othes swore
With fulle glad hert and prayn hym also
That he wolde vouchesauff to do so
And that he wolde be oure gouernoure
And of oure tales Iuge and reportoure
And sett a sopere at a certeyne pryce
And wol be reuled at his devise .
High and lowe and alle be one assent
We be accordede to the Iugement
And therevppon the wyne was fett anone
We dronke and to rest went we echone
Withoute eny lenger taryyng
